question_text: In cloud computing, what best describes Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS)?
option_a: On-demand compute, storage and networking building blocks that the customer configures and manages
option_c: A no-code app builder
option_d: Fully managed applications delivered over the web

question_text: An Azure VM is memory-bound. Which lever most directly addresses this without redesigning the app?
option_a: Changing the DNS zone
option_b: Enabling a larger font in the portal
option_c: Adding a public IP address
option_d: Choosing a VM series/size with a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio (right-sizing the SKU)

question_text: What do Azure Availability Zones primarily protect a workload against?
option_a: The failure of an entire datacentre/zone within a region
option_c: A user forgetting their password
option_d: An expired TLS certificate

question_text: In the North Cheshire & Mersey datacentre migration, how can existing Windows Server/SQL licences reduce Azure cost?
option_a: By disabling backups
option_b: By applying Azure Hybrid Benefit to reuse licences with Software Assurance on Azure
option_c: By deleting all on-premises licences immediately
option_d: By buying the largest VM available

question_text: Before migrating a datacentre to the cloud, what is the purpose of a discovery and assessment phase?
option_a: To inventory workloads, dependencies, sizing and readiness to plan migration waves
option_c: To pick a logo colour for the project
option_d: To skip planning and lift everything at once

question_text: Which Azure service provides a central hub to discover, assess and migrate servers, databases and web apps to Azure?
option_a: Azure DNS
option_c: Azure Key Vault
option_d: Azure Firewall

question_text: In cloud migration strategy, what does 'rehost' (one of the 6 Rs) mean?
option_a: Move the workload to the cloud largely as-is ('lift and shift') with minimal change
option_c: Rewrite the application from scratch as cloud-native
option_d: Repurchase a SaaS replacement

question_text: In the DHCW 'migration wave one' engagement, why sequence a datacentre migration into waves rather than moving everything at once?
option_a: Because Azure only accepts one server per day
option_c: To reduce risk by grouping workloads by dependency/complexity and validating each wave
option_d: To avoid ever assessing the estate

question_text: What is an Azure Landing Zone?
option_a: A pre-configured, governed environment (identity, networking, governance, security) that workloads land into at scale
option_c: A single virtual machine
option_d: A physical loading dock in a datacentre

question_text: What does the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) provide?
option_a: A specific VM SKU
option_c: Guidance and best practices across Strategy, Plan, Ready, Adopt, Govern and Manage for cloud adoption
option_d: A hardware warranty

question_text: A customer needs consistent policy and access control across many subscriptions. Which Azure construct helps apply governance at scale?
option_a: One giant resource group for everything
option_c: A single shared admin password
option_d: Management groups with Azure Policy and RBAC

question_text: What is the primary role of a virtual network (VNet) in Azure?
option_a: To render 3D graphics
option_b: To act as an email server
option_c: To store relational data
option_d: To provide an isolated private network for Azure resources to communicate securely

question_text: A customer needs a private, high-bandwidth, predictable connection from their datacentre to Azure that does not traverse the public internet. What should you recommend?
option_a: A site-to-site VPN over the public internet only
option_c: A public IP on every VM
option_d: Azure DNS

question_text: Why do Azure landing zones commonly use a hub-and-spoke network topology?
option_a: Because spokes cannot exist without exactly 100 VMs
option_b: To force all traffic onto the public internet
option_c: To centralise shared services (firewall, gateways, DNS) in a hub while isolating workloads in spokes
option_d: To avoid using virtual networks at all

question_text: Which Azure service provides a managed, stateful network firewall with centralised policy for a VNet/hub?
option_a: Azure Advisor
option_c: Azure Firewall
option_d: Azure Backup

question_text: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
option_a: Both only apply to networking
option_b: Authentication proves who you are; authorization determines what you can access
option_c: Authentication assigns permissions; authorization verifies identity
option_d: They are identical terms

question_text: A customer running on-premises Active Directory wants users to sign in to Azure/M365 with the same identity. Which approach enables this hybrid identity?
option_a: Synchronise on-prem AD to Microsoft Entra ID (e.g. Entra Connect)
option_c: Recreate every user manually in the cloud with different passwords
option_d: Disable identity entirely

question_text: What does Azure Arc enable?
option_a: A replacement for Power BI
option_c: A new relational database engine
option_d: Extending Azure management, governance and policy to servers/Kubernetes/data services running outside Azure (on-prem or other clouds)

question_text: In the NHS SQL end-of-support and North Cheshire engagements, how was Azure Arc used?
option_a: To replace the network cabling
option_c: To inventory and govern the existing on-prem server/SQL estate before migration
option_d: To immediately delete all servers

question_text: What is Azure VMware Solution (AVS)?
option_a: A DNS forwarding service
option_b: A service to run native VMware vSphere environments on dedicated Azure infrastructure
option_c: A Power BI connector
option_d: A container registry

question_text: In the CQC engagement, why was an Azure VMware Solution pilot proposed to migrate a Siebel CRM platform off ageing hardware?
option_a: To delete the CRM entirely
option_b: To move VMware-hosted workloads to Azure with minimal re-platforming risk, as a landing foundation
option_c: To rewrite Siebel from scratch first
option_d: To avoid using Azure at all

question_text: What is the primary purpose of Microsoft Defender for Cloud?
option_a: To provide a data warehouse
option_c: Cloud security posture management and workload protection - assessing/hardening security across resources
option_d: To manage DNS records

question_text: In disaster recovery, what does the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) define?
option_a: The colour of the status dashboard
option_b: The number of VMs in a subscription
option_c: The price of a support plan
option_d: The maximum acceptable downtime before service must be restored

question_text: How should an Infra SE best present a datacentre-exit migration plan to a non-technical executive board?
option_a: Show raw ARM templates and routing tables in detail
option_b: Send only the networking diagrams with no narrative
option_c: Focus purely on VM SKU numbers
option_d: Frame it around business outcomes - risk reduction, cost, resilience, timeline - with a clear phased roadmap
